input: Take a foraging walk in local woodland

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether the user wants to forage for fungi, berries, leaves, bark, nuts, or a mix changes what to look for, what season matters most, and what tools to bring.
Whether this is a solo walk, a family outing, or a group trip changes the pace, safety considerations, and how much guidance or supervision is needed.
The specific woodland location and the time of year determine which species are realistically available and whether permits or access rules apply.
How long the user can spend affects how far they walk, how much they can collect, and whether preparation time beforehand is feasible.
Whether the user wants a structured learning experience or a relaxed casual walk changes whether they should hire a guide, use an ID app, or bring a field guide.
Knowing whether success means correctly identifying species, actually collecting and cooking something, or simply enjoying nature shapes how ambitious the plan should be.
The user's prior foraging experience determines whether they need beginner safety briefings, identification resources, or just a reminder of what to pack.

gold.taskTitle: Take a foraging walk in local woodland
gold.taskDescription: Plan and carry out a foraging walk in a nearby woodland area to find and collect wild plants, fungi, or other edible natural materials.

questions.title: What types of things do you want to forage for?
questions.description: Identify whether the focus is fungi, berries, edible leaves, nuts, herbs, or a general mix — this determines what to look for and what season is best.

questions.title: Will you be going alone or with others?
questions.description: Establish whether this is a solo outing, a family trip, or a social group walk, as this affects safety planning, pace, and how much expert guidance may be needed.

questions.title: Which woodland and roughly what time of year?
questions.description: Pin down the specific location and season to confirm which species will be available and whether there are any land access or permit considerations.

questions.title: How much time do you have set aside for this?
questions.description: Understand the total time available — from preparation through to the walk itself — to scope the plan realistically.

questions.title: Do you want a structured learning experience or a relaxed explore?
questions.description: Determine whether the user prefers a guided, educational approach with field guides or an app, or simply a casual walk with light awareness of what they find.

questions.title: What would make this walk feel like a success to you?
questions.description: Clarify whether the goal is correctly identifying species, bringing something home to cook, or simply enjoying the experience outdoors.

questions.title: How much foraging experience do you already have?
questions.description: Gauge the user's skill level to decide whether the plan needs to include beginner safety guidance, species ID resources, or just a packing checklist.
